title: PREPOSITIONS
notes:
✓ Preposition → a word that shows the relationship between a noun/pronoun and another word in a sentence.

✓ Prepositions commonly express → time, place, direction, movement, position, cause, method, and relationship.

✓ The book is on the table.
✓ We arrived at 8:00.
✓ She walked into the room.

✓ Common prepositions → in, on, at, by, for, from, to, with, about, of, under, over, between, among, through, across, during, since, until, without.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF TIME: AT
notes:
✓ Use 'at' for a specific point in time.

✓ at 7:00
✓ at noon
✓ at midnight
✓ at night
✓ at lunchtime
✓ at the weekend (especially British English)

✓ The class starts at 8:00.
✓ I usually sleep at night.

✓ AT → exact/specific time.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF TIME: ON
notes:
✓ Use 'on' with specific days and dates.

✓ on Monday
✓ on Friday morning
✓ on August 31
✓ on my birthday
✓ on New Year's Day

✓ We have an exam on Monday.
✓ She arrived on Friday morning.

✓ ON → day/date.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF TIME: IN
notes:
✓ Use 'in' with longer periods.

✓ in August
✓ in 2026
✓ in summer
✓ in the morning
✓ in the 21st century
✓ in the future

✓ I was born in 2006.
✓ We study in the morning.

✓ IN → month, year, season, century, or longer period.

title: SINCE, FOR, DURING, UNTIL & BY
notes:
✓ since → starting point
✓ I have lived here since 2020.

✓ for → duration
✓ I have lived here for six years.

✓ during → within a period/event
✓ I slept during the movie.

✓ until/till → up to a particular time
✓ I waited until 5 p.m.

✓ by → no later than a particular time
✓ Finish the work by Friday.

✓ since = starting point
✓ for = length of time
✓ until = continues up to
✓ by = deadline

title: PREPOSITIONS OF PLACE: AT
notes:
✓ Use 'at' for a specific point or location.

✓ at the bus stop
✓ at the door
✓ at school
✓ at home
✓ at the airport
✓ at work

✓ I'll meet you at the station.
✓ She is waiting at the door.

✓ AT → a point or specific location.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF PLACE: IN
notes:
✓ Use 'in' when something is inside an area, space, or enclosed place.

✓ in the room
✓ in the box
✓ in the building
✓ in Ethiopia
✓ in Addis Ababa
✓ in the car

✓ The keys are in my bag.
✓ She lives in Ethiopia.

✓ IN → inside an area or enclosed space.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF PLACE: ON
notes:
✓ Use 'on' when something is touching or positioned on a surface.

✓ on the table
✓ on the wall
✓ on the floor
✓ on the ceiling
✓ on the page

✓ The phone is on the table.
✓ There is a picture on the wall.

✓ ON → surface/contact.

title: IN vs ON vs AT
notes:
✓ AT → point
✓ at the station

✓ IN → inside/area
✓ in the station

✓ ON → surface
✓ on the platform

✓ Time comparison:
✓ at 7:00 → exact time
✓ on Monday → day
✓ in August → month

✓ Quick rule → AT = point, ON = surface/day, IN = inside/area/long period.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF DIRECTION & MOVEMENT
notes:
✓ to → movement toward a place/person
✓ She went to school.

✓ into → movement from outside to inside
✓ He walked into the room.

✓ out of → movement from inside to outside
✓ She went out of the house.

✓ onto → movement to a surface
✓ The cat jumped onto the table.

✓ toward(s) → in the direction of
✓ He walked towards the door.

✓ through → movement from one side/end to another within something
✓ We walked through the tunnel.

title: ACROSS, ALONG, PAST & AROUND
notes:
✓ across → from one side to the other
✓ They walked across the bridge.

✓ along → following the length or direction of something
✓ We walked along the river.

✓ past → moving beyond a person/place
✓ She walked past the school.

✓ around → surrounding or moving in a circular/general area
✓ We walked around the park.

✓ These prepositions describe the path of movement.

title: ABOVE, OVER, BELOW & UNDER
notes:
✓ above → higher than something
✓ The picture is above the sofa.

✓ over → higher than; sometimes directly covering/crossing
✓ The plane flew over the city.

✓ below → lower than something
✓ The temperature is below zero.

✓ under → directly beneath or covered by something
✓ The shoes are under the bed.

✓ above/below → general higher/lower position.
✓ over/under → often closer, directly positioned, covering, or movement-related.

title: BETWEEN & AMONG
notes:
✓ between → normally used for two distinct people/things or clearly separated individuals/items.
✓ The bank is between the school and the hospital.

✓ among → surrounded by or included in a group.
✓ She was sitting among her friends.

✓ BETWEEN → distinct/separate relationships.
✓ AMONG → group or mass.

title: BESIDE, BEHIND, IN FRONT OF & OPPOSITE
notes:
✓ beside → next to
✓ She sat beside me.

✓ behind → at the back of
✓ The car is behind the house.

✓ in front of → before/in a position ahead of
✓ He stood in front of the door.

✓ opposite → facing or directly across from
✓ The bank is opposite the school.

title: PREPOSITIONS OF TRANSPORT
notes:
✓ Common expressions:
✓ by car
✓ by bus
✓ by train
✓ by plane
✓ by bicycle
✓ on foot

✓ I go to school by bus.
✓ We travelled by plane.
✓ She went there on foot.

✓ Use 'on' for many forms of public transport when emphasizing being aboard.
✓ on the bus
✓ on the train
✓ on the plane

✓ Use 'in' for smaller enclosed vehicles.
✓ in a car
✓ in a taxi

title: PREPOSITIONS OF METHOD & INSTRUMENT
notes:
✓ by → method/means
✓ We travelled by bus.

✓ with → instrument/tool used
✓ He cut the paper with scissors.

✓ by → means of communication/creation in some expressions
✓ I sent it by email.

✓ BY = method/means.
✓ WITH = tool/instrument.

title: WITH, WITHOUT & ABOUT
notes:
✓ with → together with / having / using
✓ I went with my friend.

✓ without → in the absence of
✓ He left without his phone.

✓ about → concerning a subject
✓ We talked about the exam.

✓ about can also mean approximately.
✓ It takes about two hours.

title: FOR, FROM & TO
notes:
✓ for → purpose, benefit, or duration
✓ This gift is for you.
✓ I stayed there for two days.

✓ from → starting point, origin, or source
✓ She is from Ethiopia.
✓ The train comes from Nairobi.

✓ to → destination, direction, or recipient
✓ I went to school.
✓ Give the book to him.

✓ FROM = origin.
✓ TO = destination/direction.
✓ FOR = purpose/benefit/duration.

title: PREPOSITION + NOUN / PRONOUN / GERUND
notes:
✓ A preposition is normally followed by a noun, pronoun, or -ing form.

✓ after school
✓ with him
✓ before leaving
✓ without studying
✓ interested in learning

⚠ After a preposition, use the object form of a pronoun.

❌ between you and I
✓ between you and me

✓ When a verb follows a preposition, use the gerund (-ing).

❌ She is interested in learn English.
✓ She is interested in learning English.

title: COMMON ADJECTIVE + PREPOSITION
notes:
✓ good at → She is good at mathematics.
✓ interested in → He is interested in science.
✓ afraid of → She is afraid of dogs.
✓ proud of → They are proud of their work.
✓ responsible for → He is responsible for the project.
✓ famous for → Ethiopia is famous for its history.
✓ different from → This is different from that.
✓ similar to → My answer is similar to yours.
✓ worried about → She is worried about the exam.

✓ Learn these as fixed combinations.

title: COMMON VERB + PREPOSITION
notes:
✓ depend on → Success depends on effort.
✓ listen to → Listen to the teacher.
✓ wait for → I'm waiting for the bus.
✓ look at → Look at the picture.
✓ talk about → We talked about school.
✓ belong to → This book belongs to me.
✓ agree with → I agree with you.
✓ apologize for → He apologized for being late.
✓ believe in → She believes in herself.

✓ Many verbs require a particular preposition. Learn the complete combination.

title: COMMON PREPOSITION ERRORS
notes:
❌ He is good in English.
✓ He is good at English.

❌ I am interested on music.
✓ I am interested in music.

❌ She depends of her parents.
✓ She depends on her parents.

❌ We discussed about the problem.
✓ We discussed the problem.

❌ I arrived to the airport.
✓ I arrived at the airport.

❌ I have lived here since five years.
✓ I have lived here for five years.

❌ She is married with a doctor.
✓ She is married to a doctor.

✓ Do not translate prepositions directly from your first language; learn common combinations.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. AT → exact time / specific point.
✓ at 8:00, at the station.

◆ 2. ON → days / dates / surfaces.
✓ on Monday, on the table.

◆ 3. IN → months / years / enclosed areas.
✓ in August, in 2026, in the room.

◆ 4. SINCE → starting point.
✓ since 2020.

◆ 5. FOR → duration.
✓ for five years.

◆ 6. BY → deadline / method.
✓ by Friday, by bus.

◆ 7. UNTIL → continuing up to a time.
✓ until midnight.

◆ 8. TO → destination/direction.
✓ go to school.

◆ 9. FROM → origin/source.
✓ from Ethiopia.

◆ 10. BETWEEN → distinct people/things.
✓ between A and B.

◆ 11. AMONG → group.
✓ among friends.

◆ 12. INTO → movement inside.
✓ walk into the room.

◆ 13. THROUGH → movement within/from one side to another.
✓ through the tunnel.

✓ Golden rule → Learn prepositions together with the words they commonly follow, because many combinations are fixed.
